title: Windows-Compatible Shell Command Execution
why: 30 run_shell errors last week due to invalid syntax (e.g., '&&') and missing repository checks. A dedicated skill can prevent these errors by adapting commands to Windows environment.

payload.name: windows-safe-shell
payload.description: Execute shell commands safely on Windows with proper syntax adaptation and pre-checks.
payload.body:
## Procedure
1. Translate common Unix idioms:
   - Replace '&&' with ';'. If conditional execution is needed, use 'if ($?) { command }'.
   - Replace '||' with 'if (-not $?) { command }'.
   - For pipe, use '|' but ensure proper quoting.
2. Before running git commands, verify the current directory contains a .git folder using 'Test-Path .git'.
3. Use 'cd /d D:\path' or 'Set-Location D:\path' to change drives.
4. Enclose file paths with spaces in single quotes.
5. For multi-line scripts, consider using a script block with try/catch.
6. Always check the exit code ($?) after command execution and handle errors gracefully.

title: Web Extraction with Browser Headers
why: Web extraction from news sites (Reuters) failed with 401/403 errors, likely due to missing User-Agent. A skill to set proper headers reduces such failures.

payload.name: web-extract-headers
payload.description: Fetch web content using realistic browser headers to avoid being blocked.
payload.body:
## Procedure
1. Identify the target site. If it's a commercial news site, assume it requires a User-Agent.
2. Use the following headers when calling web_extract (if the tool supports headers):
   - User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/91.0.4472.124 Safari/537.36
   - Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/webp,*/*;q=0.8
   - Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.5
3. If web_extract does not support custom headers, fall back to using Invoke-WebRequest with -Headers parameter in PowerShell.
4. Parse the response content appropriately and handle errors.
